title: Daily arXiv Biology and Biomedicine — 2026-11-06
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a popularity ranking, and arXiv's biomedical coverage is incomplete. Many clinical and experimental biology preprints appear on bioRxiv or medRxiv.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: The latest arXiv biology and biomedicine announcement batch, Friday 6 November 2026, contributes 10 notable papers selected from 22 eligible records (14 new submissions and 8 revisions). Single-cell genomics and computational discovery dominate, alongside protein-model evaluation and retrospective clinical prediction. Spoken agenda: drug-discovery agents, gene regulation, single-cell benchmarks, tissue and drug-response prediction, protein scaffolding, docking, and EHR/imaging methods. Sunday 8 November had no newer batch.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking, not a popularity ranking, and arXiv's biomedical coverage is incomplete. Many clinical and experimental biology preprints appear on bioRxiv or medRxiv.

sections.title: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
sections.abstract: PharmAgents2 combines literature-derived decision skills and parallel agents for drug-discovery investigations; the authors report three investigations with findings subsequently tested in human-executed experiments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a 121-question benchmark and three end-to-end tasks. They report experimental follow-up for an LpxH inhibitor scaffold, JAK1 inhibitor candidates, and a proposed secondary target for a known bioactive molecule.
sections.unique_caveat: Human researchers performed the experiments. The findings concern early discovery assays and do not establish clinical efficacy, safety, or therapeutic utility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct drug-discovery relevance and three author-reported experimental follow-ups; relevance and contribution signals, not measured popularity.

sections.title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
sections.abstract: MUSS joins DNA-sequence-derived representations with chromatin accessibility and paired single-cell expression data to model gene regulation across scales.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report performance against sequence and single-cell baselines for expression prediction, enhancer–gene linking, motif-guided prioritization, and zero-shot clustering, including tests involving unseen genes and peaks.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are computational, not causal evidence. The authors note dependence on a frozen sequence encoder and paired multi-omic data, quadratic attention cost, and limitations in unseen-link evaluation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct genomics fit; the arXiv record lists NeurIPS 2026; evaluated on four paired single-cell datasets and multiple downstream tasks.

sections.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
sections.abstract: BILBY adds a PROSITE-derived protein-motif benchmark and molecular-dynamics checks to test whether static motif recovery predicts dynamic scaffold behavior.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that 31/55 statically solved designs met their MD-supported criterion and 8/55 passed all checks, indicating that static refolding does not establish full-scaffold dynamical fidelity.
sections.unique_caveat: The MD thresholds are heuristic; 200 ns design trajectories may miss slower instabilities. The study is computational and does not establish biochemical function.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track); reports a 220-case benchmark and molecular-dynamics assessment of 55 statically solved model–problem pairs.

sections.title: One Method Does Not Fit All: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Imputation Methods for Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data
sections.abstract: This revised benchmark compares 16 single-cell RNA-seq imputation methods across protocols, downstream tasks, and datasets, finding that rankings depend on the task and data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that traditional methods are often more consistent across tasks, while strong numerical recovery does not necessarily improve downstream biological interpretation.
sections.unique_caveat: Benchmark outcomes depend on dataset, protocol, and analytical goal; the authors find no universally best method. The comparisons do not demonstrate true-expression recovery in every setting.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: v3 revision in the batch; broad evaluation across 16 methods, 10 protocols, 6 downstream tasks, and 30 benchmark datasets.

sections.title: Querying Counterfactuals on Tissue Graphs with Supervised Disentanglement
sections.abstract: Cellina models in-silico tissue-neighborhood interventions by separating a cell’s intrinsic state from its spatial context.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report stronger in-silico perturbation predictions than spatial and non-spatial competitors and identify cancer subdomains with distinct predicted signaling programs.
sections.unique_caveat: Counterfactual outputs are model predictions, not newly performed interventions; performance in the reported benchmarks does not establish causal validity in other tissues.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: v4 revision in the batch; evaluated in observational and interventional screens spanning more than 2.5 million spatially resolved cells.

sections.title: Thalamus-Reasoning: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Multi-Sample Omics Reasoning
sections.abstract: Thalamus-Reasoning represents bulk or single-cell transcriptomes as continuous embeddings that can be combined with language instructions and other samples.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report leading results among tested models on several held-out annotation tasks and GEO-OmicsQA variants, and best average performance among compared methods on PerturbQA.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark measures performance on curated tasks, not experimental discovery. Some training supervision is LLM-generated with task-specific quality checks; no new biological experiments are reported.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: v3 revision in the batch; includes GEO-OmicsQA, a publication-disjoint benchmark of 3,000 questions, and evaluations on annotation and perturbation-response tasks.

sections.title: scTREAT: Latent Diffusion for Single-Cell Drug-Response Prediction
sections.abstract: scTREAT uses latent diffusion with explicit cell-state, drug-identity, and dose conditioning to predict single-cell drug-response profiles.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report best scores on 10/12 metrics for unseen cell-line–drug combinations and 11/12 for unseen drugs among the compared methods.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark is computational and uses condition-level pseudobulk profiles; predicted responses need independent experimental validation and are not treatment evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: v3 revision in the batch; evaluated on condition-level pseudobulk profiles from Tahoe-100M for unseen cell-line–drug combinations and unseen drugs.

sections.title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
sections.abstract: This study tests how far back a primary-care EHR model needs to look to predict incident colorectal cancer using nested calendar-time windows.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report AUROC rising from 0.551 at a two-year lookback to 0.590 at 18 years before plateauing; XGBoost reached a similar peak of 0.589.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective prediction in one North West London health system with modest discrimination; no prospective utility is shown, so this is not a validated screening test.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted at Machine Learning for Health 2026 (Findings Track); evaluates a frozen cohort of 1,008 cases and 9,582 matched controls after pretraining on 3.6 million primary-care patients.
sections.journal_ref: Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2026, Findings Track

sections.title: Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort
sections.abstract: This revised MRI study tests whether reweighting underrepresented scanner batches before ComBat estimation reduces residual scanner effects in glioma radiomic features.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report significant residual scanner association in 13/428 features after standard ComBat versus 8/428 after batch-augmented ComBat.
sections.unique_caveat: Single-center radiomics harmonization; reduced scanner association does not establish external generalization or improved patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: v2 revision in the batch; retrospective Erasmus Glioma Database cohort of 733 patients from one center across nine scanner configurations; arXiv comments say submitted to JMRI.
sections.comment: Original article. Submitted to Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (JMRI).

sections.title: Geometric Relevance Is Not Sufficient: Evaluating Focused Post-Training Supervision in Diffusion Docking
sections.abstract: A fixed-budget DiffDock study compares broad continuation with focused torsional supervision and finds no consistent advantage for focused strategies on its reported docking endpoints.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that broad continuation had the highest mean trained-policy Top-1 success below 5 Å; focused or mixed supervision did not consistently improve success under the tested budget.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a computational result for DiffDock under one fixed training budget; it does not establish improved docking in prospective or experimental settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct molecular-docking relevance; accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop; evaluation separates score fidelity, generated-pose quality, best-of-10 sampling, and confidence-selected Top-1 performance.
sections.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD Workshop.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: The batch emphasizes single-cell genomics and learned representations: MUSS, Cellina, Thalamus-Reasoning, scTREAT, and the imputation benchmark connect expression with regulatory context, spatial context, or drug response. Evaluation is task- and context-specific in this set: the imputation benchmark spans datasets and tasks, BILBY adds dynamics beyond static recovery, docking separates pose quality from score fidelity, and the EHR study varies calendar-time context. PharmAgents2 reports human-run assay follow-up, unlike the mostly computational predictions. The EHR and MRI studies are retrospective and do not establish clinical utility.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: For MUSS enhancer–gene links, Cellina tissue-neighborhood counterfactuals, and scTREAT drug responses, pre-register predictions and test them with perturbation assays across independent cell types, separating benchmark performance from causal evidence. Extend imputation and Thalamus-Reasoning comparisons to additional protocols, tissues, and independent cohorts with task-specific uncertainty. PharmAgents2's three human-run experiments warrant independent replication and orthogonal target-engagement and selectivity testing before any therapeutic inference. Colorectal prediction and MRI harmonization need external systems, periods, hospitals, and scanners; prospective utility and patient outcomes remain untested. BILBY motivates longer or replicated dynamics simulations paired with biochemical stability/activity assays, since MD support is not experimental function.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: This batch is notable for making evaluation design central: results vary by cell type, task, dataset, temporal context, or physical criterion. PharmAgents2 offers the clearest experimental bridge, but at early discovery-assay level. The other selected findings are computational or retrospective; the papers are ranked by relevance rather than measured attention.
